title: A QR Code Can Still Scan With Part of It Missing
fb_caption: Scratched, smudged, or torn, a QR code often still works. Those little squares hold your link plus extra recovery data worked out with clever math, so if part of the code is covered your phone fills in the gaps. At the highest setting, up to about 30 percent can be restored. The three big corner squares help your camera find the code and line it up, even upside down, so cover one of those and the scan can fail. Do you scan QR codes, or type the link yourself?
engagement_comment: Do you scan QR codes, or type the link yourself? 1 = I scan everything, 2 = I type the link, 3 = only restaurant menus.

beats.text: A QR code can still scan with a chunk of it missing. Here's how.
Those little squares hold your link, plus extra recovery data worked out with clever math.
If a smudge or a tear covers part of it, your phone uses that data to fill in the gaps.
Here's the twist. At the highest setting, up to about thirty percent can be restored.
Those three big corner squares help your camera find the code and line it up, even upside down.
But if you cover one of those three corner squares, your phone may not find the code at all, and the scan can fail.
Do you scan QR codes, or type the link yourself? Tell us below.
